summary: Carol S. Anderson is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Chicago, studying under W. S. Karunatillake and John A. Brinkman, and served as Associate Professor of Religion at Kalamazoo College.

Carola Roloff works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson and Geshe Thubten Ngawang. Her posts include the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and visiting professor at Hamburg (2018–2025).
Carola S. Carstens is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her doctorate at the University of Hamburg by 2006 and held a post at Rice University from 1998 to 1999.
Carole M. Cusack is a religious studies scholar. She studied at the University of Sydney from 1988 to 1995 and held a post there in 2013.

Carole McGranahan is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. She earned her PhD at the University of Michigan under Nicholas Dirks and Ann Laura Stoler, and held a post as Assistant Professor of Anthropology at CU Boulder (~2001–2008).

Caroline Humphrey works in Iranian/Central Asian studies and religious studies. Educated at Cambridge and Leeds, she held fellowships at Girton and King's, and served as a university lecturer/professor at the University of Cambridge from 1978 to 2010.

Caroline Rhys Davids was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar. She studied at University College London under George Croom Robertson and T. W. Rhys Davids, later lecturing at Manchester (1910–1913) and SOAS (1918–1933).

Carolyn Woodford Schmidt is an art historian and Buddhist studies scholar. She earned her PhD at Ohio State University under John C. Huntington and held teaching posts at Ohio State and Denison University.
Carson T. Schütze is a linguist who earned his degree at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (1992–1997). In 1997, he held a post at the University of California, Los Angeles.

Catherine Bell was a scholar of religious studies and sinology. She studied at the University of Chicago under Joseph Kitagawa and served as the Bernard J. Hanley Professor of Religious Studies at Santa Clara University from 1985 to 2008.

Catherine Cornille is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. She studied at KU Leuven and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, later serving as Associate Professor of Comparative Theology at Boston College around 2005.
Catherine Ella Blanshard Asher was an art historian and Indologist. She earned her PhD at the University of Minnesota, where she also served as an assistant professor from circa 1984 to 2021.

Catherine Ludvik specializes in religious studies, Japanology, and Indology. She received her PhD from the University of Toronto under David B. Waterhouse, later holding positions at the Italian School of East Asian Studies and Hanazono University.

Catherine Prueitt is an Indologist, philosopher, and religious studies scholar. She earned her PhD at Emory University under John D. Dunne and Laurie L. Patton, and was appointed Assistant Professor at the University of British Columbia.
Cathy Cantwell is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Kent (~1983–1989) and held a post at the University of Oxford in 2002.

Cecil Bendall was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Cambridge under E. B. Cowell and under Theodor Benfey. He served at the British Museum, University College London, and as Professor of Sanskrit at Cambridge (1903).

Cecil Y. Lang was an academic who studied at Duke University. He held positions at Yale and the University of Chicago before serving as Professor of English at the University of Virginia from circa 1970 to 1991.

Chack-fan Lee is a scholar active in Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Hong Kong and the University of Western Ontario, he served as Pro-Vice-Chancellor at the University of Hong Kong from 1994 to 2015.
Chaesong Kim is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. Kim pursued doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo under Yasunori Ejima.

Chagdud Tulku Rinpoche was a Tibetan Buddhist figure. He studied under multiple traditional teachers, including Delog Dawa Drolma, Dzongsar Khyentse Chokyi Lodro, Tromge Trungpa Rinpoche, Dudjom Rinpoche, and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.
